notes.title: Sophie's Sweet Spot — Business Plan Summary
notes.content:
Sophie's Sweet Spot — Business Plan

Business type: Artisan bakery & café
Location: 15 Palmer Square, Princeton, NJ 08540
Opened: March 2025
Owner: Sophie Chen (sole proprietor)

Mission: Bring joy to Princeton through beautifully crafted baked goods made with premium ingredients and creative flavors.

Products:
- Artisan breads (sourdough, focaccia, whole grain)
- Pastries (croissants, danishes, scones)
- Custom cakes (weddings, birthdays, events)
- Cookies & bars
- Seasonal specials
- Coffee & espresso drinks (third-party roaster: Counter Culture)

Target market:
- Princeton residents (affluent, quality-conscious)
- University students and faculty
- Local businesses (corporate orders, catering)
- Special events (weddings, celebrations)

Competitive advantage:
- Only artisan bakery in downtown Princeton (others are chain/commercial)
- Custom cake specialty (personalized designs)
- Community feel — regulars know us by name
- Instagram-worthy presentation (great for organic marketing)

Long-term vision: Establish as Princeton's go-to bakery, potentially expand to second location in 2-3 years.

notes.title: Expansion Plans — Second Location Research
notes.content:
Second Location Research — EXPLORATORY (2027-2028 target)

Potential locations:
1. Cranbury, NJ (15 min south)
   - Pros: No artisan bakery, growing community, lower rent
   - Cons: Less foot traffic, would need car-dependent customers
   - Estimated rent: $2,500/month

2. Lawrenceville, NJ (10 min west)
   - Pros: Near Princeton but more affordable, strip mall with parking
   - Cons: Less charm, more competition
   - Estimated rent: $3,000/month

3. Princeton Junction (train station area)
   - Pros: Commuter traffic, grab-and-go potential
   - Cons: High rent, fast-paced (doesn't fit our vibe)
   - Estimated rent: $4,500/month

Requirements before expansion:
- [ ] First location consistently profitable for 6+ months ($4K+ monthly profit)
- [ ] Systems documented (recipes, processes, training manuals)
- [ ] Manager hired for first location (so I can focus on new one)
- [ ] $30K savings for buildout and first 6 months operating costs
- [ ] Loan from bank or investors (est. $50-80K needed)

Timeline:
- 2026: Focus on growing current location, document systems
- 2027 H1: Research locations, secure financing
- 2027 H2: Buildout and opening

This is a dream but I need to be smart about it. First location first.

notes.title: Bakery Financials — Profit & Loss
notes.content:
Sophie's Sweet Spot — P&L Summary (March 2026 projected)

Revenue:
- Walk-in sales: $8,500
- Custom cakes: $3,500
- Corporate orders: $2,500
- Online/delivery: $800
- Total revenue: $15,300

Cost of Goods Sold (COGS):

- Packaging: $400
- Total COGS: $3,150 (21% of revenue)

Gross profit: $12,150 (79% margin)

Operating expenses:
- Rent: $2,800
- Employee payroll + taxes: $7,167
- Utilities: $350
- Insurance (business): $200
- Marketing: $400
- Software (POS, Gusto, etc.): $150
- Maintenance/supplies: $200
- Miscellaneous: $150
- Total operating expenses: $11,417

Net operating profit: $733
Sophie's draw: $3,500
Net after draw: -$2,767

Wait — how does this work?
- I only draw $3,500 in months where accumulated cash allows it
- January was break-even, February I could draw because Valentine's was big
- Some months I draw less ($2,500-3,000) to keep cash buffer
- Running a bakery is not yet paying me a real salary
- But trajectory is positive! Each month revenue grows.

Break-even (including my target $4K/month draw): Need $19,000/month revenue
Current trajectory to break-even: June-July 2026 at current growth rate
